summary: One basket can hold goods from several shops and is paid for once, but nothing after that payment is shared, so the model is a parent order that holds the payment and the address, and a sub-order per shop that holds everything which can still move: accepted, preparing, shipped, delivered, returned, disputed. The money is exact because the parent is a sum rather than a share. Every figure — the line totals, a discount, the shop's delivery charge, the platform's commission — is computed and stored on the sub-order it belongs to, and the order's grand total is the sum of those, so nothing is distributed proportionally, nothing has to be rounded, and nothing can fail to add up; two check constraints hold it, one saying a sub-order's buyer total is its items less its discount plus its delivery, the other saying the platform's cut and the shop's payout together are exactly that. A basket stores quantities and never a price: what it costs is read from the catalogue each time it is opened, because a price somebody saw last week is not a price they are owed. Everything becomes fixed at one point, `placeOrder`, which re-reads every line against the shop, the offer, the stock and the delivery charge, states in plain words whatever moved since the buyer last looked, refuses to go on unless the buyer has confirmed the exact figure about to be charged, and then writes the order, its sub-orders, its item snapshots and the holds on every line in one transaction. That transaction is also the oversell guard: if the last bag went to somebody else a moment ago the whole order rolls back rather than being half-placed, and the test runs two checkouts at the same instant against a single unit and asserts one order exists afterwards. The amount charged is never in the browser — `createBatch` reads it from the order row, exactly as an animal deposit is read from its deal — and the holds become sales only inside the transaction that moves the payment attempt out of PENDING. Because the effect lives there, a replayed callback, a second tab and a provider retry all arrive to find the work done; nothing here detects a duplicate, which is why nothing here can fail to. A failed payment keeps the order and its holds so the same order can be paid again rather than a second one being made. Afterwards the shops are genuinely independent: one refusing, running out of time or being argued with cancels and refunds its own part, returns its own goods to the shelf through the inventory ledger, and leaves the rest of the order exactly where it was. Silence past the acceptance deadline is a refusal — but only where a deadline exists, because an unconfigured window must not become an automatic cancellation. A seller sees their own sub-order and the name, telephone and address a parcel needs; what else was in the basket, which other shops were in it and what the whole order came to are not there, and the test compares the whole shape of that contact so any field added to an order later cannot quietly reach a seller.

domainConfigUi.newSuite: tests/domain/commerce-orders.test.ts — 16 tests on the arithmetic and the state machine, because those are where being quietly wrong costs somebody money: a line and its discount, an unstated delivery charge not being free delivery, a commission truncating in the shop's favour and capped at the sale, a sub-order's two shares being the whole of it, an order total that is the sum of awkward figures with nothing unaccounted for, a refund being the whole of one shop's part including its delivery, who may move what from where, a parent that says only what is still true of the whole order, a changed basket being shown while an unbuyable one stops the checkout, a confirmation being of one exact figure, a deadline that does not exist not making anything overdue, and the seller's contact shape compared key by key.

database.newSuite: tests/db/commerce-orders.test.ts — 11 tests, each building two real trading stores and paying at the gateway stub: one basket across two shops paying once and becoming two sub-orders whose figures sum exactly to the payment, a shop that never stated a delivery charge being refused by name and clearing once it states zero on purpose, a price that moved between the basket and the gateway stopping the checkout with nothing written and nothing held, two simultaneous checkouts for the last unit leaving exactly one order and one live hold, a callback replayed twice leaving one SELL movement and one order, a failed payment keeping the order and its holds for a retry that then succeeds, an abandoned order putting the goods straight back, one shop missing its deadline cancelling and refunding only its own part while the other stands where it was, a shop unable to read or move another's sub-order or to open the whole order, the walk from accepted to delivered to returned with the goods counted back through the ledger and the refund opened, and the item rows staying what was bought after the shop repriced everything.

limitations: There is no discount source yet. The order, the sub-order and the item rows each carry their own discount column and the arithmetic subtracts it correctly wherever it appears, but nothing in the product can put a non-zero figure there: shop promotions and coupons are PROMPT-012. The allocation is tested with non-zero discounts in the domain suite rather than being claimed end to end.

Settlement is not built. Each sub-order freezes the commission the store agreed to and records what the store is owed, but paying that out is PROMPT-011, and the settlement hold and cadence settings are still NOT_CONFIGURED.

The refund record is opened automatically and executed by hand. A cancelled or returned sub-order writes what is owed the moment it is owed, and executing it uses the same retrying machinery and the same operator queue the animal deposit already had — including MANUAL_REQUIRED where a gateway has no refund call.

Nothing runs on a timer. Unaccepted sub-orders are swept when an operator opens the order queue, expired holds are released when a line is read, and `cancelExpiredOrders` exists for a caller that does not exist yet. This is the same honest limitation the listing expiry and the deposit deadline carry.

A dispute on a sub-order is a status with a reason and a history, not the evidence workflow the animal market has. Whether shop disputes need that shape is PROMPT-013's question, and building half of it here would have been a guess.

A partial return is modelled — the item row carries a returned quantity — but only a whole sub-order can be returned through the screens. Returning some lines and keeping others needs a per-line refund figure, which is the same arithmetic as a discount and belongs with it.
The delivery address is snapshotted onto the order and prefilled from the profile's residence. There is no address book: one would be speculative until somebody has ordered twice.
